meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him before they did?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

I'm writing down September 24, 380 words, forty minutes. Show me that piece next to the essay, because I read documents myself. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before that zero went in.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay. The checker is off the table, and I'm writing that down. What does the version history show, Hale? I want dates and times, not a summary.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed in the meeting to take the detector score off the table. I still expect the zero withdrawn, and I still need the September 24 writing sample and the version history, each with dates and times, along with an answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at the opening position, wanting the zero withdrawn and an apology, with nothing yet shown to her and no answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
What moved her: dropping the detector score got a flat okay and a note in her pad, and the September 24 sample with exact numbers made her ask to see it, but she moved no further because she had seen nothing she could check.
What cost ground: nothing cost ground outright, but you never answered whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in, and that left her main grievance standing untouched.
Try next time: right after conceding the detector, own in one sentence that the zero went in before you called home, then put the version history with its times in front of her.
